name: Lemon-Garlic Shrimp Orzo with Asparagus
description: A fast one-skillet dinner: orzo toasted and simmered in broth like a quick risotto, with asparagus and garlicky shrimp stirred in at the end. On the table in about 25 minutes.
ingredients: 1.5 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined (frozen is fine)
1 bunch asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1-inch pieces
Pinch of red pepper flakes (optional, adults only)
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season with half the salt and the pepper.
In a large deep skillet, melt 1 Tbsp butter with the oil over medium-high. Cook the shrimp 1–2 minutes per side until just pink. Move to a plate.
Lower to medium. Add 1 Tbsp butter and the garlic; cook 30 seconds. Add the orzo and toast, stirring, 2 minutes.
Pour in the broth and the remaining salt. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 8 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Stir in the asparagus, cover, and cook 3–4 minutes more until the orzo is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Off the heat, stir in the last Tbsp butter, the lemon zest and juice, parmesan, and the shrimp. Add pepper flakes to the adult bowls.
tips: Frozen shrimp thaws in about 10 minutes in a colander under cold running water.
Don't overcook the shrimp in step 2 — they warm through again at the end.
Chop shrimp into small pieces for the toddler; plain buttered orzo works for the baby.
Peas or baby spinach can stand in for the asparagus.
